newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI PROPERTY RIGHTS TRADE BOOMS IN JULY 1997.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI PROPERTY RIGHTS TRADE BOOMS IN JULY 1997.

text.p: Trading value on Shanghai's property rights exchange surged in July to 669 million yuan ($80.6 million), up 13.87 times from the year-earlier month, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.
Trading value of state firms' property rights was 126 million yuan in July, accounting for 18.8 percent of the total trading value, the newspaper said.
Collective enterprises' property rights trading generated 260 million yuan in July, or 38.9 percent of the total, it said.
The remaining value of 283 million yuan, or 42.3 percent of the total, was traded in other types of firms, it added, but gave no further details.
A common property rights exchange had been set up in late July along the Yangtze River delta to enable its 10 member cities to trade idle assets, the newspaper has said.
The market aimed at a trade turnover of 20 billion yuan ($2.41 billion) in 1997, the newspaper said. The 10 member cities, mostly in east China, included Shanghai, Suzhou, Wuhan and Xiamen, it said.
The establishment of the common market would attract more investors and provide good conditions for industrial restructuring, it said.
China now had a total of around 5 trillion yuan in idle assets, official media has reported.
